text: Home / News / MLB MLB Report: Cubs, Teruaki Satō Agree to Six-Year, $120M Deal The Cubs reportedly agreed to a six-year, $120 million contract with NPB Triple Crown winner Teruaki Satō, adding elite left-handed power. World Baseball News Editorial Team November 24, 2026 , 2 min read Share on X Facebook Photo: Samurai Japan / Sports Bull The Chicago Cubs are finalizing a six-year, $120 million contract with Japanese slugger Teruaki Satō, according to multiple reports, adding the 2026 Central League Triple Crown winner to an offense that led Major League Baseball in runs last season. ESPN first reported the agreement on Tuesday, November 24. The Cubs have not yet confirmed the deal, which is expected to be completed after the usual physical and contract formalities. Satō, 27, arrives after the best season of his six-year Nippon Professional Baseball career with the Hanshin Tigers. The left-handed hitter batted .306 with 39 home runs and 106 RBIs in 143 games, leading the Central League in all three categories. He also posted a .383 on-base percentage and a .609 slugging percentage. Satō gives Chicago elite left-handed power Power was the defining trait of Satō’s game in Japan. He hit 167 home runs across six seasons with Hanshin and produced an .854 career OPS, earning five All-Star selections. His 2026 Triple Crown followed a 2025 season in which he hit .277 with 40 homers and 102 RBIs and won the Central League MVP award. The Cubs are expected to use Satō in a corner-outfield role, although most of his recent defensive work came at third base. He played 125 games at third and 18 in the outfield for Hanshin in 2026. That versatility gives Chicago options around Gold Glove third baseman Alex Bregman and an outfield being reshaped around National League MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong. Satō also appeared for Japan at the 2026 World Baseball Classic, going 3-for-10 with three doubles in five games. His combination of international experience, left-handed power and positional flexibility made him one of the most prominent players available through the posting system this offseason. Cubs commit $240 million in two days The reported agreement comes less than a day after Chicago reached a five-year, $120 million deal with left-hander Trevor Rogers. Together, the two moves represent a $240 million commitment as the Cubs try to maintain a contender that led MLB in scoring in 2026. Satō’s move is also a major transition for Hanshin. text: Home / News / NPB NPB Teruaki Sato Set for MLB Posting After NPB Triple Crown Season Hanshin will post Teruaki Sato to MLB after the Tigers star won the 2026 Central League Triple Crown with 39 homers and 106 RBIs. World Baseball News Editorial Team October 20, 2026 , 2 min read Share on X Facebook Photo: Junichi Ueyama / Nikkan Sports The Hanshin Tigers will approve Teruaki Sato’s move to Major League Baseball through the posting system this offseason, putting one of Japan’s most accomplished power hitters on the international market after a Triple Crown season. Sato, who turns 28 before the 2027 season, led the Central League with a .306 batting average, 39 home runs and 106 RBIs in 2026. The left-handed-hitting third baseman is also positioned as a leading candidate for a second straight Central League MVP award after winning the honor in 2025. What the posting decision means Hanshin’s approval is the first essential step, but Sato will not become available to MLB clubs until the posting process is formally opened. Once he is posted, all 30 MLB teams will have 45 days to negotiate a contract with him. Because Sato is older than 25 and has completed more than six professional seasons, he will not be limited by MLB’s international amateur bonus pools. He can sign a major-league contract of any length and value, while the Tigers would receive a release fee based on the guaranteed value of the deal. If Sato does not reach an agreement during the 45-day window, he would return to Hanshin for the 2027 season and could not be posted again until the following offseason. Sato brings proven power and durability Sato’s 2026 performance confirmed the progress he made a year earlier. He hit 40 home runs with a .924 OPS in 2025, earning Central League MVP honors and a Golden Glove at third base. Across six NPB seasons, he has topped 20 home runs five times and produced a career .851 OPS. His power is the defining tool, but his profile is not without risk. Sato struck out in roughly 27 percent of his plate appearances over the past two seasons, a figure MLB clubs will weigh against his home-run production and improving plate discipline. He also drew walks in 10.3 percent of his plate appearances during that span. Durability strengthens his case. Sato has appeared in at least 120 games in every NPB season, and he has experience beyond Japan’s domestic schedule. He helped Hanshin win the 2023 Japan Series and represented Samurai Japan at the 2026 World Baseball Classic

text: Home / News / NPB NPB Teruaki Sato Becomes First Shigeo Nagashima Award Winner Hanshin Tigers star Teruaki Sato became the inaugural Shigeo Nagashima Award winner after a .306, 39-homer, 106-RBI Triple Crown season. World Baseball News Editorial Team November 12, 2026 , 1 min read Share on X Facebook Photo: Nikkan Sports Hanshin Tigers third baseman Teruaki Sato was named the first winner of the Shigeo Nagashima Award on Thursday, November 12, adding a new national honor to a 2026 season in which he captured Nippon Professional Baseball’s batting Triple Crown. The award was introduced this year in memory of the late Yomiuri Giants legend Shigeo Nagashima. It recognizes an NPB position player whose running, hitting and defense stand out while also exciting fans and contributing to baseball’s cultural reach. A new award begins with Sato Sato was selected by a five-member committee featuring Sadaharu Oh, Koji Yamamoto, Akinobu Okada, Hideki Kuriyama and Kazuo Matsui. The 27-year-old will receive the trophy at the NPB Awards ceremony on November 25. Oh, the committee chair, said the panel wanted the inaugural choice to establish a standard worthy of Nagashima’s name. Sato’s combination of production, presence and all-around impact made him the first player attached to the new honor. Triple Crown season separated Sato Sato played all 143 games for Hanshin and finished with a .306 batting average, 39 home runs and 106 RBIs, leading the Central League in all three categories. He also recorded 165 hits, 100 runs, 40 doubles, a .383 on-base percentage and a .609 slugging percentage. The season made Sato the ninth Triple Crown winner in NPB history and the first Japanese player to achieve the feat for Hanshin. His power in the heart of the order helped the Tigers win a second consecutive Central League pennant. Sato’s year was not limited to offense. He also won the Central League Gold Glove at third base, giving the selection committee another measure of the complete season envisioned by the award’s criteria. The Nagashima Award will not necessarily be presented every year; it is reserved for a player the committee considers to meet its full standard. By choosing Sato after a championship season and one of the strongest individual campaigns in recent Japanese baseball, the panel gave the new prize an immediate benchmark. text: Home / News / NPB NPB Liván Moinelo and Teruaki Sato Capture 2025 NPB MVP Honors Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks ace Livan Moinelo and Hanshin Tigers star Teruaki Sato are named 2025 Pacific and Central League MVPs in NPB. World Baseball News Editorial Team December 17, 2025 , updated September 15, 2026 , 3 min read Share on X Facebook Hanshin Tigers star Teruaki Sato watches his hit during his MVP-winning 2025 Central League season in Nippon Professional Baseball. Nippon Professional Baseball crowned two dominant stars at its annual awards ceremony, naming Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks ace Liván Moinelo the 2025 Pacific League Most Valuable Player and Hanshin Tigers slugger Teruaki Sato the 2025 Central League Most Valuable Player . The selections reflect a season defined by elite pitching dominance and overwhelming offensive production at the highest level of Japanese baseball. Liván Moinelo: A Historic MVP for the Pacific League After an outstanding transition from elite reliever to frontline starter, Liván Moinelo authored one of the most dominant pitching seasons in recent NPB history. Already excellent in 2024, the Cuban left-hander took another leap in 2025, separating himself from every other pitcher in the Pacific League. Moinelo finished the season with a microscopic 1.07 ERA , leading all NPB starters, while striking out 150 batters in 143.1 innings . He threw three complete games , including the first two shutouts of his NPB career , and posted a 29-inning scoreless streak during the heart of the season. His advanced metrics further illustrate the dominance: first in WHIP (0.87) , first in ERA+ (278) , second in strikeout rate (27.8%), and among league leaders in innings pitched, batting average against, and shutouts. These numbers place Moinelo squarely in the conversation with peak seasons from Yoshinobu Yamamoto , underscoring just how rare his 2025 campaign was. The MVP award also puts him on the brink of history, no Cuban-born player has ever won an NPB league MVP or the Eiji Sawamura Award , Japan’s equivalent of the Cy Young. Moinelo now stands as the leading candidate to achieve both. At 29, firmly in his prime, Moinelo has established himself not only as the cornerstone of the SoftBank rotation but as one of the greatest foreign pitchers ever to compete in NPB. text: Home / News / NPB NPB Teruaki Sato Delivers Again as Hanshin Tigers Cut Central League Magic Number to 12 Teruaki Sato delivered the go-ahead hit and Kotaro Otake threw seven scoreless innings as the Hanshin Tigers beat Hiroshima 2-1 and cut their magic number to 12. World Baseball News Editorial Team September 18, 2026 , 2 min read Share on X Facebook Photo: Kato Yasu / Nikkan Sports Teruaki Sato delivered the go-ahead hit for the second straight night and Kotaro Otake threw seven scoreless innings as the Hanshin Tigers beat the Hiroshima Toyo Carp 2-1 at Koshien Stadium on Friday, September 18, tightening their grip on the Central League pennant race. The victory moved Hanshin to 71-57-1 and reduced its magic number to 12 with the regular season entering its final stretch. Sato, already in the middle of a career season, drove a fourth-inning single through the right side to break a scoreless tie. Sato delivers another decisive hit Hanshin opened the fourth against Hiroshima starter Masato Morishita with consecutive baserunners before Sato came to the plate with nobody out and runners at first and second. The Tigers cleanup hitter lined a 1-1 pitch into right field to score the game’s first run. Yusuke Oyama followed immediately with another RBI single, giving Hanshin a 2-0 advantage. The two runs proved to be enough. Sato’s hit gave him the winning RBI for a second consecutive game and his 19th game-winning RBI of the season. He entered Friday batting .315 with 35 home runs and 94 RBIs, keeping him at the center of both Hanshin’s pennant push and the Central League’s individual leaderboards. Otake shuts down Hiroshima Otake gave the Tigers exactly the kind of start they needed in a tight September race. The left-hander held Hiroshima to two hits across seven scoreless innings, striking out five and earning his sixth victory of the season. Morishita kept the Carp within reach, allowing only four hits and two runs over seven innings while striking out eight, but Hiroshima’s offense could not generate enough against Otake. The Carp finally broke through in the eighth. Shogo Akiyama’s groundout brought home a run and cut the deficit to 2-1, but Hanshin’s bullpen prevented the tying run from scoring. Taisei Kudo closed the ninth for his 10th save. Hanshin keeps control of the Central League race The win was Hanshin’s second in a row over Hiroshima after a 7-2 victory on Thursday and came at an important point in a close pennant race.
